claims.text: A Mo-based graded alloy can be used as an interlayer to effectively bond W and CuCrZr.
A Mo-based graded interlayer reduces residual thermal stresses in bonded W/CuCrZr.
A Mo-based graded interlayer improves adhesion between W and CuCrZr under fusion-reactor conditions.
Directly bonded W and CuCrZr exhibit a significant thermal-expansion mismatch.
Thermal-expansion mismatch causes degradation of the direct W/CuCrZr interface under extreme temperatures and irradiation.
The proposed intervention is to place a Mo-based graded-alloy interlayer between W and CuCrZr.
Fusion-reactor operation subjects the joint to high thermal loads, substantial thermal cycling, and neutron irradiation.
The graded chemical composition of the Mo-based alloy provides a thermal-expansion response intermediate between those of W and CuCrZr.
The Mo-based graded alloy provides high thermal conductivity between W and CuCrZr.
The Mo-based interlayer bridges the mismatch between the thermal-expansion coefficients of W and CuCrZr.
Bridging the thermal-expansion mismatch reduces residual stress during thermal cycling.
The Mo-based interlayer enhances interfacial adhesion.
The Mo-based interlayer maintains mechanical stability under neutron irradiation.
Relative to direct bonding, the interlayer will improve W/CuCrZr interface integrity and bonding durability.
Relative to direct bonding, the interlayer will enable effective heat transfer across the W/CuCrZr joint.
Direct W-to-CuCrZr bonding suffers from poor adhesion and residual-stress buildup caused by thermal-expansion mismatch.
The benefit may be limited if the Mo-based alloy is not optimally graded.
The benefit may be limited if operating temperature or neutron flux exceeds the interlayer's tolerance.
The required Mo-based alloy composition and gradation have not been determined.
The magnitude of improvement is uncertain without experimental validation.
